plan.contextChunk: This figure places two drawings of the same circuit side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them. Each is a rectangle split by a single vertical wire into two adjacent loops. Two blue zigzag resistor symbols sit along the top wire, labeled R1 = 3.00 ohms on the left and R3 = 3.00 ohms on the right. The dividing branch carries R2 = 3.00 ohms and the right-hand vertical wire carries R4 = 4.00 ohms, while the left-hand vertical wire is a plain conductor. Two battery symbols sit along the bottom: V1 = 24.00 V in the left loop, plus terminal on the left, and V2 = 29.00 V in the right loop, plus terminal on the right. Panel (b) repeats every element unchanged and adds six teal dots at the corners and branch points, lettered a, b, and c across the top and f, e, and d across the bottom. Setting the bare circuit beside the lettered copy separates the physical layout from the labels laid over it. The pair prepares a multi-loop network for analysis with Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules, the two points where three wires meet serving as the junctions.

interactionPlan.concept: Kirchhoff's rules turn one multi-loop circuit into solvable equations: at each junction the currents balance, and around any closed loop the signed voltage rises and drops sum to zero — node labels a–f are bookkeeping laid over an unchanged physical circuit.
elements: single rectangular circuit frame split by a center vertical branch into two loops (the interactive shows one drawing whose caption swaps between (a) and (b) instead of two side-by-side panels)
resistor R1 = 3.00 Ω (blue zigzag) on the top wire of the left loop, between a and b
resistor R3 = 3.00 Ω (blue zigzag) on the top wire of the right loop, between b and c
resistor R2 = 3.00 Ω (blue zigzag) on the shared center branch, between b and e
resistor R4 = 4.00 Ω (blue zigzag) on the right vertical branch, between c and d
plain left vertical wire between a and f
battery V1 = 24.00 V on the bottom wire of the left loop, + terminal on the left
battery V2 = 29.00 V on the bottom wire of the right loop, + terminal on the right
six teal node dots at a, b, c (top) and f, e, d (bottom), visible in labeled mode
node letters a, b, c, d, e, f beside their dots, visible in labeled mode
caption '(a)' or '(b)' beneath the circuit, matching the toggle
current arrows labeled I1, I2, I3 on the three branches meeting at the selected junction (junction mode)
junction equation annotation 'I1 = I2 + I3' (junction mode)
loop-trace traversal highlight that visits each element in order (loop mode)
equation strip accumulating signed voltage terms and ending in 'ΣΔV = 0' (loop mode)

interactions.label: Circuit view
interactions.teaches: Node dots and letters are analysis scaffolding laid over the same physical circuit — toggling shows that every resistor, battery, and wire is identical; only the naming needed for Kirchhoff's rules is added
At a junction the currents in the three connected branches must balance — clicking b or e highlights those branches, draws current arrows, and shows I1 = I2 + I3 (current in equals current out)

interactions.label: Loop tracing
interactions.teaches: Walking a closed loop in one direction assigns each element a signed term — a rise across a battery traversed − to +, a drop across a resistor traversed with the current (a rise against it) — and the accumulated terms must total zero

demo_steps.title: The bare circuit
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a) shows the physical circuit: two loops sharing the middle branch R2, with V1 = 24.00 V (+ terminal left) in the left loop and V2 = 29.00 V (+ terminal right) in the right loop. Nothing here is labeled yet.

demo_steps.title: Labels are scaffolding
demo_steps.narration: Switching to panel (b) adds teal dots and letters a–f at the corners and branch points — but not a single component changes. The labels exist only so Kirchhoff's rules can name places; b and e are the junctions where three wires meet.

demo_steps.title: Junction rule
demo_steps.narration: Click junction b (or e): its three branches highlight, current arrows appear, and the junction equation I1 = I2 + I3 states that whatever current flows in must flow back out.

demo_steps.title: Loop rule — left loop
demo_steps.narration: Trace the left loop a→b→e→f→a: each element lights in traversal order as its term is added — a drop I1R1 across R1, a drop I3R2 down R2, a rise of V1 = 24 V through the battery — building an equation that must sum to zero.

demo_steps.title: Loop rule — right loop
demo_steps.narration: Trace the right loop b→c→d→e→b: the shared branch R2 now contributes a term of the opposite sign because the traversal goes against I3, and V2 enters as a drop when crossed from + to − — loop direction is what sets the signs.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The labels a–f change nothing physically — they exist so Kirchhoff's two rules can be written down: currents balance at junctions b and e (I1 = I2 + I3), and signed voltage changes sum to zero around either loop.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw one circuit, not two panels: a rectangle split by a center vertical branch into two equal loops. Blue zigzag resistors: R1 and R3 along the top (left and right of center), R2 on the center branch, R4 on the right vertical; left vertical is a bare wire. Battery symbols on the bottom of each loop with long/short plates and +/− marks: V1 + on the left, V2 + on the right. Component labels in italic serif styling exactly as 'R1 = 3.00 Ω', 'V1 = 24.00 V', etc. In labeled mode, small teal dots appear at all six corners/branch points with lowercase italic letters a, b, c across the top and f, e, d across the bottom; the caption beneath swaps from (a) to (b) — fade the dots/letters in rather than cutting. Junction-click mode: highlight the three branches meeting at the clicked junction in amber, overlay colored current arrows (I1 entering b from the left, I2 leaving toward c, I3 downward through R2), and place the equation I1 = I2 + I3 nearby. Loop-trace mode: a moving highlight dot travels the chosen loop clockwise, each resistor/battery flashes amber as reached, and a term chip ('+24.0 V', '−I1·3.00 Ω', …) is appended left-to-right in an equation strip below the circuit, closing with 'ΣΔV = 0' once the loop completes; the shared branch R2's term flips sign between the two loops.

authoredContext:
Consider the circuit in the figure(a). Let us analyze this circuit to find the current through each resistor. First, label the circuit as shown in part (b).

(a) A multi-loop circuit. (b) Label the circuit to help with orientation.

Part a shows a circuit with two horizontal branches and three vertical branches. The first horizontal branch has two resistors of 3 Ω each and the second branch has two voltage sources of 24 V with positive terminal on the left and 29 V with positive terminal on the right. The left vertical branch is directly connected, the middle branch has a resistance of 3 Ω and the right branch has a resistance of 4 Ω. Part b shows the same circuit as part a with labelled junctions

Next, determine the junctions. In this circuit, points b and e each have three wires connected, making them junctions. Start to apply Kirchhoff’s junction rule (∑ Iin=∑ Iout) by drawing arrows representing the currents and labeling each arrow, as shown in the figure(b). Junction b shows that I1=I2+I3 and Junction e shows that I2+I3=I1. Since Junction e gives the same information of Junction b, it can be disregarded. This circuit has three unknowns, so we need three linearly independent equations to analyze it.

discrepancies: in the loop-trace equation chips the right-loop traversal labels the R₄ term as 'I₄·4.00 Ω', but the junction-rule layer only defines currents I₁, I₂, I₃ — the source-level two-loop model uses the same three branch currents throughout

the labeled view (b) shows node letters and teal junction dots but does not reproduce the full letter placement style of the source panel (b) (letters directly at corners/branch points with no dots in the source); minor, since the toggle correctly implements the (a)/(b) split
resistor zigzags are thinner and smaller relative to the loop than in the source, where the resistor glyphs are bold and visually dominant; the circuit still reads correctly

the source places '(a)' and '(b)' captions beneath two side-by-side panels; the generated figure shows only one panel with a toggle — acceptable per multipanel-toggle convention, but the default view is noticeably sparser than either source panel
evaluation.notes: A faithful single-panel reproduction of the two-loop Kirchhoff circuit with correct topology, polarities (V₁ + on left, V₂ + on right), and correct values, plus genuinely strong pedagogy: an (a)/(b) label toggle, clickable junctions with the KCL equation, and animated loop traces that build the KVL equation term by term — the only real blemish is the inconsistent I₄ current label in the right-loop trace.
action_items: In the right-loop trace terms, change '−I₄·4.00 Ω' to '−I₂·4.00 Ω' (or relabel the junction arrows to define I₄) so the loop equation uses the same three branch currents as the junction rule.
Bold the resistor zigzags (stroke width ~3.5) and slightly increase their amplitude so the components visually dominate the wires as in the source.
In labeled view, place node letters flush at the corner/branch points (as in panel b) rather than offset around dots, or drop the dots to match the source more closely.

In labeled view, place node letters flush at the corner/branch points (as in panel b) rather than offset around dots, or drop the dots to match the source more closely.

discrepancies: in the loop-trace equation chips the right-loop traversal labels the R₄ term as 'I₄·4.00 Ω', but the junction-rule layer only defines currents I₁, I₂, I₃ — the source-level two-loop model uses the same three branch currents throughout

the labeled view (b) shows node letters and teal junction dots but does not reproduce the full letter placement style of the source panel (b) (letters directly at corners/branch points with no dots in the source); minor, since the toggle correctly implements the (a)/(b) split
resistor zigzags are thinner and smaller relative to the loop than in the source, where the resistor glyphs are bold and visually dominant; the circuit still reads correctly

the source places '(a)' and '(b)' captions beneath two side-by-side panels; the generated figure shows only one panel with a toggle — acceptable per multipanel-toggle convention, but the default view is noticeably sparser than either source panel
kimi-k3.notes: A faithful single-panel reproduction of the two-loop Kirchhoff circuit with correct topology, polarities (V₁ + on left, V₂ + on right), and correct values, plus genuinely strong pedagogy: an (a)/(b) label toggle, clickable junctions with the KCL equation, and animated loop traces that build the KVL equation term by term — the only real blemish is the inconsistent I₄ current label in the right-loop trace.
action_items: In the right-loop trace terms, change '−I₄·4.00 Ω' to '−I₂·4.00 Ω' (or relabel the junction arrows to define I₄) so the loop equation uses the same three branch currents as the junction rule.
Bold the resistor zigzags (stroke width ~3.5) and slightly increase their amplitude so the components visually dominate the wires as in the source.
In labeled view, place node letters flush at the corner/branch points (as in panel b) rather than offset around dots, or drop the dots to match the source more closely.
